questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to stay close to Copenhagen, Denmark, where I study law at full time. I therefore wanted to find a city, with a good culture, nice study environment and that was close to Denmark by airplane. I had always heard many great things about Milan, including the study environment, and therefore that led to me research the city even more!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would recommend everyone going!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, however, there are some aspects that were quite hard to find out unless you knew someone who had the answer or someone who had gone to Milan a former semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think when I arrived I had a hard time trying to figure out the deadlines of, for example, registration for courses and exams - but it did work out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used AirBnB and it was very easy!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive. I would recommend trying to find something within a walking distance of the school as many classes are at different times during the day (I had a 2 km walk each way and that was perfect).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was room in every class that one wanted to join or register in, and it was very easy to find information.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was easier than what we are used to in CPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The level is different than the one in Copenhagen, and the teaching method is also different. There is much less readings and preparation for each class, however the teacher does expect that you are active in class and that you are an attending student.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Competition law and economics
European monetary and economic law
Law and policies of social rights protection in the EU
Public and private partnerships for sustainable development
Smart cities, AI and digital transformation law

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to use ESN activities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Please go see the other cities that are very close!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Milan is a fantastic city, which is very easy to feel at home in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the ESN events, go to local bars and meet people!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of eating out, the culture of being open-minded and open to meeting new people (like us Danish people) etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: (1) Prepare yourself for a different teaching method, (2) please find accommodation that is close to the university and the center, and (3) be prepared to spend a lot of money on going out/ being social.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: he public transportation does not work after 00:30 until 05:00 (only night busses), so keep that in mind when finding housing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New academic challenges and new friends!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to live in another city.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
